To show that beef tallow is acceptable for use in a cosmetic product, manufacturers must establish and maintain records sufficient to demonstrate that the tallow contains no more than 0.15 percent insoluble impurities as determined by AOCS Official Method Ca 3a-46 or an equivalent method, and that it is not derived from prohibited cattle materials. These records must be retained for 2 years after creation. When filing entry with U.S. Customs and Border Protection, the importer of record must affirm that the cosmetic was manufactured from, processed with, or otherwise contains cattle material and was manufactured in accordance with this section, and if requested, must provide records within five days to demonstrate the absence of prohibited cattle materials. The evidence does not contain any requirement to hold lots in quarantine until verified.

21 CFR 700.27(a)(6) requires tallow to be produced from tissues that are not prohibited cattle materials or must contain no more than 0.15 percent insoluble impurities as determined by AOCS Official Method Ca 3a-46 or an equivalent method [8].  
21 CFR 700.27(c)(1) requires manufacturers and processors of a cosmetic that is manufactured from, processed with, or otherwise contains material from cattle to establish and maintain records sufficient to demonstrate that the cosmetic is not manufactured from, processed with, or does not otherwise contain prohibited cattle materials [14].  
21 CFR 700.27(c)(2) requires that such records must be retained for 2 years after the date they were created [15].  
21 CFR 700.27(c)(6) requires, when filing entry with U.S. Customs and Border Protection, that the importer of record affirm that the cosmetic was manufactured from, processed with, or otherwise contains cattle material and was manufactured in accordance with this section, and if requested, must provide records within five days to demonstrate the absence of prohibited cattle materials [17].
